 Early voting expands Monday in Chicago, suburban Cook County and across the suburbs 
 Photo identification is not required but it can be helpful if there is a question about voter registration, address or signature. 
 By Matt Stefanski, NBC Chicago Staff and Michelle Baik • 
 Published October 18, 2026 • 
 Updated 2 hours ago 
 BOOKMARKER 
 NBC Universal, Inc. 
 Starting Monday, residents in Cook County, Chicago and elsewhere across the region will have more early voting options. Michelle Baik reports.
 With Election Day just over two weeks away, Cook County voters will have more options for casting their ballots beginning Monday.
 Early voting expands to all 50 wards in Chicago, while suburban Cook County increases from six locations to 56. Chicago residents can cast their ballots at any early voting site in the city, while suburban Cook County voters can use any suburban location.

 Ahead of the Nov. 3 election, Cook County Clerk Monica Gordon demonstrated the tools her office will be using, including an electronic poll book known as a Poll Pad.
 Officials will extract data from Poll Pads through a new analytics platform called Election Lens, which monitors election activity in real time across suburban Cook County.
 FULL LIST: Early voting locations in suburban Cook County 
 Cook County Clerk Monica Gordon said she's already received more than 200,000 requests for mail-in ballots. Gordon said her office is expanding the ability to track those ballots from the time they’re first printed all the way until they return.
 “We know voters want confidence that their mail ballot is moving through the process, as it should," Gordon said. "Election Lens will now incorporate U.S. Postal Service scanning information, giving our team greater visibility into where mail ballots are in the process and how long they have been at each stage...”

 Residents can also register to vote at all suburban Cook County early voting sites.
 Photo identification is not required, but it can be helpful if there is a question about voter registration, address or signature.
 There’s also another opportunity for voters casting mail-in ballots: they can be placed in a drop box at Soldier Field. Mail-in ballots can also be returned to designated drop boxes at polling locations.
 And the early voting expansion isn't limited to Chicago and Cook County. 
 Other sites are also opening on Monday in DeKalb, DuPage, Kendall, Lake, McHenry and Will counties. 
 Additional information about voting by mail, polling places and more can be found on the Illinois State Board of Elections website.
